headline: Failed House bill would have placed the Smithsonian American Women's History Museum on a specific National Mall site and set content rules.
what_it_does: The bill would have named the South Monument site on the National Mall, across from the National Museum of African American History and Culture, as the museum's location, though the President could have picked another site within 180 days. Control of the land would have moved to the Smithsonian, which would have needed approval from federal bodies such as the Commission of Fine Arts to design and build the museum and would have paid the costs of that approval process. The museum would have been dedicated to the history and experiences of biological women, and it could not have depicted any biological male as a female. Its advisory council would have had to seek guidance from sources reflecting a range of political viewpoints.

who_it_affects.how: It would have gained control of the museum site and been required to get federal approvals and cover the costs of the building approval process.
They would have been required to seek guidance from a broad range of sources with differing political views when creating or substantially changing exhibits and programs.
The museum would have been barred from presenting or depicting any biological male as a female.
Undeveloped land on the Mall would have been set aside for a new museum building.
